attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given as his own assertion within his critique of Newton.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the three uses Marcus names. It is a plain past-tense observation with no hedge, quantifier or horizon. The 'and so on' does not add any testable content.

contract.note: The plain reading (each use documented by the post date) is fair and ordinary. The broad reading of 'AI' matches how the post uses the word. The 2019 start date is reasonable. The ambiguity over whether AI 'made' or 'drove' denials does not change the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI threat report, May 2024, on covert influence operations using its models for deceptive content. It is a company disclosure, but the contract accepts company threat reports, and it is about misuse by third parties. It establishes the misinformation use. Low reach does not matter to the claim.
Official FBI advisory dated 2024-12-03, before the post. It says criminals use generative AI for fraud. It establishes the scams use.

Trade-association summary of the October 2024 Senate PSI report. It says AI and predictive tools (e.g. naviHealth/nH Predict) produced more post-acute care denials in 2019-2022. The contract accepts summaries of primary documents. It establishes the insurance-denial use, though it is secondhand.

News report on the nH Predict lawsuit. UnitedHealth denies the tool makes coverage decisions. That qualifies the claim but does not refute the Senate finding that the tools drove more denials. The date is inferred, not shown.

reviews.rationale: All three named uses are documented before 2024-12-06: misinformation (OpenAI report, e1), scams (FBI advisory, e2) and insurance denials (summary of the Senate report, e3). UnitedHealth's denial (e4) is a self-interested dispute and does not meet the contradiction condition. The claim is only that the uses happened, so it is supported.
